observations.body: Paul argues that law arriving 430 years after promise does not annul it, says law was added because of transgressions, ordained through angels by a mediator, and cannot give life.
observations.label: Promise, law after 430 years, angels, and mediator

observations.body: Promise, law after 430 years, angels, and mediator belongs to sinai remembered in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: Galatians 3:15–22 supplies later-memory evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: Later witnesses select and reuse Sinai in their own settings; they remain later readings rather than replacements for the Exodus event.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read Galatians 3:15–22 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: Promise, law after 430 years, angels, and mediator belongs to the sinai remembered movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
payload.title: Promise, law after 430 years, angels, and mediator
